sub_palette: near_eastern (old_persian / axsatran backbone) + classical (hellenic / achillean overlay) - cross-family blend, Persian-leaning

blend.backbone: near_eastern (old_persian / axsatran register: the Xshayathiya and his satraps, Old-Persian phonology, ezafe-linked construct, Arta the Truth and the farnah-glory, theophoric on the shifted canon-stems Turvasa-/Urlaspa-/Arta-)
blend.overlay: classical (hellenic / achillean: the polis and the agora, the strategos and the basileus, the sea-faring craft, Greek -os/-on civic and learned vocabulary, aspirates th/ph/kh, the heroon and the mysteria)
blend.lean: Persian-heavy - the satrapal court of the King of Kings sits over the Greek poleis of the coast: the Old-Persian throne, road and fire-order rules; the Hellenic city, harbour and school endure and serve beneath. Persepolis and Athens in one crown - the satrap and the polis fused.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_04 Axsatra (Achaemenid Persia, near_eastern + old_persian register) x BASE_07 Achillea (Classical Greek, classical + hellenic). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: both parents are Civilized, so Hellaria is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Greco-Persian realm - the Hellenistic-Achaemenid synthesis, a Seleucid-Persian court where the satrapy and the polis are one people. Backbone/lean = Persian (the satrapal throne, the Old-Persian court register, the Arta/farnah religion, the land-and-kin and rule vocabulary); overlay/substrate = Greek (the coastal poleis, the agora and harbour, the sea/civic/learned/material vocabulary, the philosophic schools). Common-word lexicon is a SINGLE fused tongue (Persian-shaped, Greek-substrated) per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md; rank titles use the real Old-Persian and Greek registers (allowed, catalog 5.3), with English display titles and an approved foreign term where set. DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Old-Persian-shifted Sargonid morphs PRIMARY per axsatran, Hellenic morphs SECONDARY per achillean), never real Iranian/Greek gods. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic. Approved foreign display terms: kingdom = Shah (Persian); county = Archon (Greek) - recorded in approved_foreign_terms_used.

phonology.palette: Old Persian (Indo-Iranian) backbone - flowing vowels a i u with long a/i/u, spirants th(0)/x(kh)/f, sibilants s/sh/z/c, r l, nasals m n, semivowels y v/w, aspirate h, characteristic endings -a/-ah/-iya/-ana/-aspa/-arta/-farnah, the ezafe genitive-of-relation '-ahya' - meeting a Hellenic overlay: Greek civic and sea vocabulary (-os/-on/-eus), the aspirates th/ph/kh (shared with Persian), open vowel-final syllables. Per the CSV: pitch accent with flowing vowels, the Greek pitch adapted to Persian vowel-flow and poetic stress; grammar SOV with complex aspects carried on the ezafe construct-chain. Theophoric on the Old-Persian-shifted canon morphs (Turvasa-, Urlaspa-, Arta-) with Hellenic devotional variants (Tulrio-, Orlandro-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV(C); Persian clusters (xsh-, sp-, st-, fr-, vr-, thr-) meeting Greek clusters (kt, pt, st, ps, ph, th, kh); vowel length distinctive; ezafe '-ahya' linking; pitch-accent flowing vowels with a Persian heavy-syllable pull; Greek -os/-on civic endings persianized to -a/-ah on the fused stems.

sound_changes: Greek civic/nominative endings persianize: -os>-a, -on>-a/-ah, -eus>-ava, -e>-a; roots become vowel-final on the Persian -a/-ah pattern
Greek pitch accent adapted to Persian flowing vowels and poetic/heavy-syllable stress; the genitive ezafe '-ahya' links construct-chains
shared aspirates th/ph/kh retained from both parents; Greek ps/pt/kt simplify toward Persian onsets (ps>s, pt>t, kt>xt); Greek double-s>sh (thalassa>thalasha)
Persian spirant/sibilant inventory dominant: collapse to a i u (long a/i/u), s/sh/z/c, x(kh), f; very short Greek roots take a Persian -a/-ah ending
fusion_rules.source_tilt: sea/civic/learned/material words from Greek roots (the coastal poleis, the harbour, the agora, the schools, marble/wine/oil); rule/kin/court/land words from Persian roots (the satrapal throne, the bloodline, the road and the fire-order, terrain and staple); every root then filtered to one Persian-shaped phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Greek sea/civic/learned/material roots + Persian rule/kin/court/land roots, all run through one Old-Persian-shaped sound-law (Greek -os/-on persianized to -a/-ah, pitch adapted to flowing vowels, shared th/ph/kh kept); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. No slash forms - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Persian satrapal nobility keep filiation 'X-ahya puthrios' (son of X) or compact 'X-puthrios' and a house (vith-X); the Greek city-folk keep the Hellenic patronymic on the fused stem (-ida, from -ides) plus a polis demonym; the throne fuses both - a Xshayathiya who also carries a polis-founder's name; theophoric given names on the shifted god-stems and on Arta-.
morphology.compounding_rule: Persian quality/relation + element via the ezafe '-ahya' (Arta-xshaca truth-realm, Vahu-farnah good-glory) layered over Greek civic compounds persianized ([adjective|resource] + feature with the old Greek linking -o- flattened: Nea-pola new-city, Spaita-akra white-cape); toponyms Dida-[name] (fort of), [name]-pura / [name]-pola (city of), Atash-[power] (fire of); the capital Persephyra (the Persian-Greek throne-seat).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Greco-Persian court: the Xshayathiya / Shah at the crown over the Greek poleis of the coast, the satraps and strategoi as his great vassals, the eparch-archons over the cities, the magi tending the fire and the philosophers the schools, both serving beneath the throne)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Persian-lean ladder with the Hellenic co-titles fused beneath, ascending. Vispati (clan-lord of a vis) barony; Marzapana (march-warden, the marzban) march; Eparch-Framatar (the appointed city-governor, Greek eparch + Persian framatar) county - DISPLAYED as Archon (the approved Greek term); Xshacapavan-Strategos (the satrap who is also the general of the poleis) duchy over a satrapy; Vispuhra-Dynastes (prince of the blood and dynast) principality over a great province (Dahyu); Xshayathiya (king) kingdom over a Xshacam - DISPLAYED as Shah (the approved Persian term); Xshayathiya Xshayathiyanam (King of Kings) empire over the Vispa-Dahyu, all the lands. The Greek cities keep their archon and strategos beneath the Persian crown; the magi (Magu) and the philosophic schools stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old-Persian and Greek registers (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Mathishta-Diadochos (the greatest successor-designate; Persian mathishta + Greek diadochos)

vassalage.vassal: Bandaka (the king's bondsman) / Symmachos (the allied city)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except where an approved commonly-known foreign term is set in 'ruler': kingdom = Shah (Persian), county = Archon (Greek). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric on the shifted god-stems or an Arta-/Vahu- virtue-name) + filiation (X-puthrios) or Greek patronymic (-ida); nobles add a house (vith-X) and a court/satrapal or polis office; the renowned earn an honest-deed or descriptive epithet; order given-first.
surname_source: office (satrap, marzban, archon, strategos) or polis demonym
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Persian court-and-satrapal nobility carry a house (vith) and a satrapal office; the Greek city nobility carry a polis demonym and a Hellenic patronymic (-ida); commoners of either stock use filiation/patronymic + earned epithet; the throne fuses both.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names from the shifted deity-stems + a Persian or Greek element: Baga-X (god-X), X-data (X-given), X-farnah (glory-of-X), Vahu-X (good-X) on the Persian side; Tulrio-, Orlandro-, Numeno- compounds on the Hellenic side. e.g. Turvasa-data, Baga-Urlaspa, Artafarnah, Tulriokles, Orlandroteron.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - the Old-Persian-shifted Sargonid morphs PRIMARY (family_near_eastern via axsatran: Turvasa, Urlaspa, Naumana, Arzanta, Asturna), the Hellenic morphs SECONDARY (family_classical via achillean: Tulrios, Orlandros, Numenos), never real Iranian/Zoroastrian or Greek gods. Lawful henotheist but TOLERANT, as the Persian backbone: Asturna the Wise Lord most high upholds ARTA (Truth/Right-order) and the Lawful powers are His yazata-ministers; the Chaotic powers are the hosts of DRAUGA (the Lie). The empire shelters the Greek city-cults under Asturna's peace - the polis keeps its mysteria and heroon beside the fire-altar. Alignment all three (per the standard human pass).
religion.the_one: Asturna (< Aeternus / Sargonid Itarnu; Greek reflex Aiternos - the Wise Lord Most High, upholder of Arta and source of the king's farnah-glory, revered above His ministers, honored not petitioned)

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Turvasa (Greek Tulrios) - the sun and Arta, lamp of right-order; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Urlaspa (Greek Orlandros) - the iron-oath, war and the cavalier; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Numeno: Naumana (Greek Numenos) - the good mind, wisdom and the law; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Argentus: Arzanta (Greek Argenthos) - trade, the road and the harbour; Lawful
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Riyata (Greek Rialthe) - the Lady of Waters, mother and mercy

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers under Asturna the Wise Lord - Turvasa the just, Urlaspa of the sworn war, Naumana of wisdom, Arzanta of the road and harbour, Riyata the merciful - keeps Arta (Truth) as the cardinal virtue and names the Chaotic powers the hosts of Drauga the Lie, warded; the fire-altar and the polis-temple uphold the right-order alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the honest dead and the just kings kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and the deified founders kept as Heros at the heroon; the great powers invoked at the Atash fire-altar and the city mysteria situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the hosts of Drauga - and names Asturna and the Lawful powers as the tyrant-order to be defied; the Lie set against the Truth.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, the hosts of Drauga the Lie (warded as daeva or marked -daimon in the Greek cities), keep their shifted name + a hostile portfolio-epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhsha the Burner-of-Cities (Greek Maraxos the Tyrant-Flame); Vacidus -> Vakida the Devouring-Void (Greek Vakidos the Unmaker); Lusanto -> Lusanta the Coin-Serpent, the Lie made gold.

clergy_ladder.5: Magupati (chief magus of a fire-temple) / Archiereus
clergy_ladder.9: Magupatan Magupat (the chief of chief magi) / Megas Hierophant

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Atash ([fire] of [power]) and its fire-temple (Atashana) on the Persian side - 'the Atashana of Turvasa'; the Mysteria/Temenos of [power] on the Greek side - 'the Mysteries of Numenos'; the magi keep the ever-burning fire (Atar) on the altar while the polis keeps its temenos.
religion.saints_pattern: the honest dead and the just kings kept as fravashi (fore-spirits) and petitioned at the fire-altar - 'the Arta-true [name]' (the righteous [name]); and the deified founders kept as Heros [name], venerated at a heroon (tomb-shrine) in the Greek cities.

holy_symbol_motifs.Asturna: a winged ring-disc (the farnah-glory) above a fire-altar, ringed by an olive-branch
holy_symbol_motifs.Turvasa: a rayed sun above the upright Arta-measure and the scales
holy_symbol_motifs.Urlaspa: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring
